scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: DeFi replaces intermediaries (banks, brokers, exchanges) with smart contracts: public programs on a blockchain that hold assets and follow fixed rules. The stack, bottom to top: Three properties make DeFi powerful and dangerous: Risk-first rule: before comparing returns, list what could make you lose money. A higher yield means you're being paid to carry more risk, whether or not the website mentions it. Blockchain: records every balance and transaction (Ethereum, layer twos, other chains). Smart contracts: the protocol logic (a lending market, an exchange pool). Tokens: the assets the contracts move. Wallets: where you hold keys and sign actions. Interfaces: websites that build transactions for you. They're a convenience, not the protocol itself.
scenes.cap: Blockchain: records every balance and transaction (Ethereum, L2s, other chains). Smart contracts: the protocol logic (a lending market, an exchange pool). Tokens: the assets the contracts move. Wallets: where you hold keys and sign actions. Interfaces: websites that build transactions for you. They're a convenience, not the protocol itself.

scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: Data layers: explorers and dashboards you use to verify what happened. Self-custody: nobody can freeze your funds, and nobody can recover them either. Composability: protocols plug into each other. That makes products powerful, and a position can fail because of something it depends on. Transparency: you can verify everything on-chain. Transparent doesn't mean safe.

lines: Is a website the same thing as the protocol?
scenes.sub: Answer: No. The interface only builds transactions. The contracts are the protocol, and interfaces can be faked or compromised.
